items.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022
items.q: let’s say you’re working on a Sinatra date, which I did many times

ctx.x: Am I correct that you would manipulate the tape over the heads so that you would hear —

Absolu— yes. No, I’ll tell you what, you want pressure? You’re working on a — at Capitol, I’m working on a Peggy Lee date or something. And as a second engineer you’re running the machines. And then the producer says, “But could we keep the first chorus on that take and go to take twelve” or whatever, “and put that second chorus together.” And usually it’s the second engineer who is running the machines that does the editing if he’s good. And I mean if you’re working at Capitol or Columbia they expect those…
make a dumb edit and you screw it up you look like a fool. Don’t look like a fool, tell them to get the hell out of the room so you can hear what you are doing.
